name: Holzgau
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Lechtal valley with colorful farmhouses and the world-famous wooden bridge leading to the waterfall.
beschreibung:
Overview

Holzgau is located at an altitude of 1,103 metres in the upper Lech Valley in the district of Reutte, affectionately known as the "Pearl of the Lechtal" thanks to its exceptionally charming townscape. The village extends across the alluvial fan of the Höhenbach stream between the Lechtal and Allgäu Alps, home to around 400 residents. Holzgau is celebrated internationally for its stately historical townhouses adorned with elaborate Lüftlmalerei fresco paintings—an architectural legacy of prosperous emigrant merchants. A modern engineering sensation is the Holzgau Suspension Bridge, opened in 2011/2012: Spanning 200.5 metres across the Höhenbach Gorge at a dizzying height of 110 metres, it forms a thrilling highlight of the Lechweg long-distance trail, seamlessly uniting alpine wilderness, architectural splendour, and mountain heritage.

History

Permanent settlement in the upper Lechtal began during the 14th century, spearheaded by Alemannic settlers arriving from neighbouring Vorarlberg and the Allgäu. The locality was first officially documented in 1315 as Holzgaw, referring to a wooded river floodplain. Because agricultural yields on high-altitude mountain soils were meagre, generations of locals worked as itinerant merchants and seasonal workers across Germany, Switzerland, and the Netherlands. Many amassed considerable fortunes abroad and returned home to rebuild their ancestral estates, commissioning talented artisans such as Josef Anton Schuler to decorate facades with vivid Baroque and Rococo frescoes. The Parish Church of Our Lady's Assumption, featuring late-Gothic foundations, was expanded and redecorated in rich Rococo style during the 18th century.

Getting There

Holzgau enjoys good transport connections by road and bus. Motorists coming from the north take the toll-free route via Füssen and Reutte, continuing along the B198 Lechtal federal highway through Elbigenalp straight to Holzgau. During the snow-free summer months, drivers can also access the village from Vorarlberg via the Bregenzerwald and Warth. Train travellers arrive at Reutte in Tirol or Füssen railway stations, connecting smoothly to the regional bus service (line 110), which runs regularly through the Lech Valley.

Tips

Crossing the Holzgau Suspension Bridge is an unforgettable adventure, offering exhilarating downward views into the rugged canyon and panoramic vistas of surrounding peaks. The trail continues into the romantic Höhenbachtal valley toward the thundering Simms Waterfall, originally engineered in the late 19th century by British industrialist Frederick Richard Simms, and the idyllic Café Uta. Heritage enthusiasts should embark on a walking tour to admire the exquisite Lüftlmalerei frescoes adorning historic houses throughout the village centre. In winter, meticulously groomed cross-country ski tracks span the valley floor alongside tranquil winter walking paths.
